newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OATES REPORTS TO CAPITALS WITH PROMISE OF NEW DEAL.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-OATES REPORTS TO CAPITALS WITH PROMISE OF NEW DEAL.

text.p: Veteran centre Adam Oates reported to the Washington Capitals Tuesday with the promise that his new team will talk about a new contract in the off-season.
Oates, who was part of a big six-player trade Saturday between the Boston Bruins and Washington, had refused to report to the Capitals without a renegotiated contract.
Oates sat out Sunday's 2-0 loss to the last-place Islanders. But he agreed to join the Capitals Tuesday after team officials agreed to talk about a lucrative long-term contract after the season.
"Our hope is that he will be so successful here that they will be offering a whole lot more in July than they would have had to offer me now," Oates' agent Brian Cook said.
"This is truly an exciting day in the history of the Washington Capitals franchise," team chairman Abe Pollin said Tuesday in announcing that Oates was on board.

"We have secured a lineup that features all-stars Peter Bondra, Adam Oates, Phil Housley, Dale Hunter and Bill Ranford. This roster makes us an immediate contender for the 1997 Stanley Cup playoffs," Pollin said.

The star centre was traded by Boston, along with goaltender Ranford and right wing Rick Tocchet, in exchange for goalie Jim Carey, centres Anson Carter and Jason Allison and a 1997 third-round draft pick.
The 34-year-old Oates, one of the NHL's premier centres, has 18 goals and 52 assists in 63 games this season.

The 12-year veteran, who played for Detroit and St Louis before being traded to Boston during the 1991-92 campaign, has 730 career assists and 254 goals. He led Boston in scoring in each of his five seasons there.

He became disenchanted with Boston's failure to contend for a Stanley Cup in recent years and publicly blasted Bruins officials last month, leading to the stripping of his assistant captain's role and heightened trade speculation.
"(The Capitals) have a good team, great defence. That's how you win Cups and I am looking forward to it," Oates said.
The Caps have been struggling offensively all season and are currently two points out of the final Eastern Conference playoff spot with 55 points.
